newsitem.title: UK: GEC shares gain on merger news.
newsitem.headline: GEC shares gain on merger news.

text.p: Shares in Britain's General Electric Company Plc (GEC) spiked higher on Friday after the company said that it and Alcatel Alsthom intended to look at the possible merger of GEC Alsthom and Framatome, traders said.
The merger would establish a group with the capability to produce both nuclear and conventional power generating plant and enhance the development potential of the two companies, GEC said.
Shortly after the announcement shares in GEC had gained 9-1/2p to 390p.

A merger between their joint venture industrial plant maker GEC Alsthom and Framtome, the nuclear reactor builder in which Alcatel has a 44 percent stake would be subject to all appropriate regulatory and other approvals, GEC said.
"This was unexpected and the degree to which the French have given them the go ahead is very unexpected and very positive," said one analyst who preferred not to be named.
There were clearly cost savings and beyond that was likely to accelerate a divestment and public offering of GEC Alsthom itself at some stage said the analyst.

"Anything that can be done to put GEC Alsthom back on a growth track - earnings really have slowed down materially in the last 12 to 18 months - or to increase the value of GEC Alsthom overall has got to be well received by the market," said the analyst.
"Particularly as this has been perceived at times as being a bit of a passive stake," he added.
